The provost has asked for a year-over-year academic performance comparison between Fall 2013 and Fall 2014. We need to identify courses that were offered in both semesters and compare their enrollment numbers, assignment counts, and average submission scores.

Please query the learning management system data to find courses with course codes ending in "2013J" and "2014J". Match courses that share the same prefix (for example AAA-2013J and AAA-2014J are the same course offered in different years) — only include a course prefix when it exists in both semesters. For each matched pair, compare the enrollment (total_students), the number of assignments, and the average submission score. The average submission score is the mean of all non-null submission scores in the course (i.e. a simple average over every graded submission, not a per-student average).

Create an Excel file called Year_Over_Year_Comparison.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be named "Course Comparison" with columns Course_Name (the common course name without the year suffix), Fall_2013_Enrollment, Fall_2014_Enrollment, Enrollment_Change (2014 minus 2013), Fall_2013_Assignments, Fall_2014_Assignments, Fall_2013_Avg_Grade (rounded to 2 decimal places), Fall_2014_Avg_Grade (rounded to 2 decimal places), and Grade_Change (2014 avg minus 2013 avg, rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort rows alphabetically by Course_Name. The second sheet should be named "Summary" with two columns, Metric and Value, containing these rows: Courses_Compared (number of course pairs), Avg_Enrollment_Change (average of all enrollment changes, rounded to 1 decimal), Avg_Grade_Change (average of all grade changes, rounded to 2 decimal places).

Create a Word document called Academic_Year_Comparison.docx in the workspace. The document should have the title "Fall 2013 vs Fall 2014 Academic Performance Review" followed by a narrative paragraph for each course pair describing the enrollment and grade changes. Conclude with a summary paragraph.

Create a Google Sheet titled "Academic Year Comparison" with a sheet called "Comparison Data" containing the same data as the Excel Course Comparison sheet.

nodes.text:
You are gathering year-over-year academic performance data from the Canvas LMS for a Fall 2013 vs Fall 2014 comparison. All data must be read via Canvas API tools (mcp__canvas__*). Do NOT write or modify anything.

CONTEXT: The provost wants to compare 6 course pairs offered in both Fall 2013 (course codes ending in "2013J") and Fall 2014 (codes ending in "2014J"). The matched pairs (same prefix, both semesters exist) are:

1. AAA: Applied Analytics & Algorithms — AAA-2013J (course id=1), AAA-2014J (course id=2)
2. BBB: Biochemistry & Bioinformatics — BBB-2013J (id=3), BBB-2014J (id=4)
3. DDD: Data-Driven Design — DDD-2013J (id=9), DDD-2014J (id=10)
4. EEE: Environmental Economics & Ethics — EEE-2013J (id=13), EEE-2014J (id=14)
5. FFF: Foundations of Finance — FFF-2013J (id=16), FFF-2014J (id=17)
6. GGG: Global Governance & Geopolitics — GGG-2013J (id=20), GGG-2014J (id=21)

For EACH of the 12 courses (ids: 1,2,3,4,9,10,13,14,16,17,20,21), compute and report:
- course_id
- course_code
- course name (e.g. "Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)")
- total_students (from the course object — use the value of the total_students field returned by canvas_get_course or canvas_list_account_courses)
- assignment count: number of assignments in the course (use canvas_list_assignments for the course and count the returned assignments; ignore quiz-type entries only if they are not assignments — count what the assignments endpoint returns)
- average submission score: the MEAN of ALL non-null submission scores in the course, i.e. sum of every graded (non-null score) submission across ALL assignments in the course divided by the count of such submissions. This is a simple average over every graded submission, NOT a per-student average. IMPORTANT: only include submissions whose score is not null; do not count unsubmitted/null-score submissions in either numerator or denominator.

HOW TO GET SUBMISSION SCORES: For each course, list assignments (canvas_list_assignments with course_id). Then for each assignment, use canvas_list_assignment_submissions (course_id, assignment_id) to retrieve submissions and their scores (note the API returns summary totals and paginated submissions). Collect every submission's score, drop nulls, accumulate sum and count. The canvas_list_student_submissions endpoint (course_id, student_ids=['all']) can also bulk-fetch submissions across assignments per course — use whichever is more efficient, but ensure you capture scores for ALL assignments in the course and that you page through until pagination.has_more is false if applicable.

DELIVERABLE: Return a concise structured summary, one line per course, with exactly these fields: course_id | course_code | total_students | assignment_count | avg_submission_score (mean of all non-null submission scores, unrounded or rounded to 6 decimals for precision). Also report the total number of graded (non-null) submissions and the sum of scores you used for each course so the calculation can be verified. Keep the response compact — a table plus brief notes on any anomalies (e.g. assignments with zero submissions, missing data).
Gather Canvas course metrics

Use the mcp__excel__* tools (create_workbook, rename/create worksheets, write_data_to_excel, format_range as needed). The workbook must have exactly two sheets.

SHEET 1 — name: "Course Comparison"

Data rows (already sorted alphabetically by Course_Name; use these exact values, numbers as numbers, grades rounded to 2 decimals as shown):

/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-course-comparison-word/workspace/Academic_Year_Comparison.docx

Use the mcp__word__* tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph). The document content must be EXACTLY as specified below, in this order:

1. TITLE (use add_heading, level 1, text): "Fall 2013 vs Fall 2014 Academic Performance Review"

2. SIX NARRATIVE PARAGRAPHS, one per course pair, in this exact order (use add_paragraph for each):

Paragraph 1: "Applied Analytics & Algorithms enrolled 383 students in Fall 2013 and 365 students in Fall 2014, a decline of 18 students. The average submission score slipped from 69.43 to 68.60, a drop of 0.83 points, while the course offered 6 assignments in both semesters."

Paragraph 2: "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics enrolled 2,237 students in Fall 2013 and 2,292 students in Fall 2014, an increase of 55 students. The average submission score fell sharply from 78.92 to 65.74, a decline of 13.18 points, and the number of assignments dropped from 12 in Fall 2013 to 6 in Fall 2014."

Paragraph 3: "Data-Driven Design enrolled 1,938 students in Fall 2013 and 1,803 students in Fall 2014, a decline of 135 students. The average submission score improved from 69.59 to 71.53, a gain of 1.93 points, while the course offered 7 assignments in both semesters."

Paragraph 4: "Environmental Economics & Ethics enrolled 1,052 students in Fall 2013 and 1,188 students in Fall 2014, an increase of 136 students. The average submission score rose from 80.63 to 82.46, a gain of 1.83 points, while the course offered 5 assignments in both semesters."

Paragraph 5: "Foundations of Finance enrolled 2,283 students in Fall 2013 and 2,365 students in Fall 2014, an increase of 82 students. The average submission score improved from 77.14 to 78.72, a gain of 1.58 points, while the course offered 13 assignments in both semesters."

Paragraph 6: "Global Governance & Geopolitics enrolled 952 students in Fall 2013 and 749 students in Fall 2014, a decline of 203 students. The average submission score fell from 80.26 to 79.08, a drop of 1.18 points, while the course offered 10 assignments in both semesters."

3. CONCLUDING SUMMARY PARAGRAPH (last paragraph):
"Across the six courses offered in both Fall 2013 and Fall 2014, average enrollment declined by 13.8 students per course, and average submission scores fell by 1.64 points. Three courses grew enrollment (Biochemistry & Bioinformatics, Environmental Economics & Ethics, and Foundations of Finance) while three declined (Applied Analytics & Algorithms, Data-Driven Design, and Global Governance & Geopolitics). Grade performance improved in Data-Driven Design, Environmental Economics & Ethics, and Foundations of Finance, and declined in the other three courses; the largest change was the 13.18-point drop in Biochemistry & Bioinformatics, which also halved its assignment count from 12 to 6."
